title: Authenticated Principal Session Architecture
objective: Define a canonical authenticated PrincipalId session model and a narrow adapter over the existing Astro session infrastructure while preserving session fixation protection, explicit expiry, fail-closed session validation, separation from River OS operator authentication, and separation from Sesh creator authorization.

infrastructure.rule: Reuse the existing generated Astro session infrastructure rather than introducing a parallel KV namespace or session database.

model.name: AuthenticatedPrincipalSession
model.sessionIdentityRule: The transport/session container remains distinct from PrincipalId.

fixationProtection.requirement: Astro session regeneration MUST occur before storing authenticated PrincipalId after credential authentication.

lifecycle.create: Regenerate transport session, validate payload, store canonical PrincipalId session with TTL.
lifecycle.read: Validate stored payload and expiry before returning identity.
lifecycle.malformed: Delete malformed authenticated-principal payload and return unauthenticated.
lifecycle.expired: Delete expired authenticated-principal payload and return unauthenticated.

riverOsBoundary.rule: River OS operator/shared-key authentication MUST NOT become PrincipalId authentication and the PrincipalId session MUST NOT reuse river-os-authenticated.

disabledPrincipal.model: Session payload alone does not prove the principal remains enabled.
disabledPrincipal.requirement: Any protected identity-resolution boundary must re-resolve AuthenticatedPrincipal and reject disabled principals before granting product access.

seshAuthorization.rule: A valid PrincipalId session proves authentication only. It does not establish SeshCreatorId, project ownership, collaborator authorization, publishing rights, or management rights.

nextSlice.title: Authenticated Session Principal Resolution Boundary
scope: Define a provider-neutral authenticated-session principal resolver.
Load PrincipalId from the canonical authenticated session.
Destroy or invalidate stale authenticated-principal sessions when canonical principal state is invalid.
Return canonical PrincipalId only after session and principal validation.
Do not create public login or registration endpoints yet.
Do not create PrincipalId to SeshCreatorId mapping.
Do not expose creator-owned Sesh APIs.
Do not mutate production identity data.
